title: Show link previews, music, polls and other app messages in the timeline export instead of [App message]
description:
Show app messages (link previews, Apple Music shares, polls, and the other "app balloon" types) in the timeline (Markdown) export, instead of the placeholder `*[App message]*`. Justin picked this as option c on 2026-11-07's work-pick question ("build your own recommended option, and the others too if time allows", relayed 2026-11-14). Today the BubbleComponent::App arm of format_timeline_message in imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs prints the message text or `*[App message]*`.

## Approach (decided)
- Reuse upstream's decision tree: call `dispatch_app_balloon(self_or_formatter, msg, &attachments, self.config)` from imessage-exporter/src/exporters/shared/balloon.rs, and implement upstream's `BalloonFormatter` trait (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/formatter.rs) for the timeline. Do NOT construct a TXT exporter to borrow its output (TXT::new creates export state with side effects), and do NOT re-parse payloads by hand.
- Content parity with the TXT exporter: each method shows the same fields, in the same order, that upstream's TXT template for that balloon shows (imessage-exporter/src/exporters/txt/balloons.rs and txt/templates/balloons/*.txt). Reuse upstream's shared helpers and view models wherever TXT does (e.g. resolve_check_in_footer, rewrite_fitness_receiver).
- Markdown shape: the balloon starts with one italic type label line (`*Link*`, `*Music*`, `*Poll*`, `*Apple Pay*`, `*Check In*`, `*Find My*`, `*Location*`, `*App Store*`, `*Collaboration*`, `*Fitness*`, `*Slideshow*`, `*Business*`, `*Handwriting*`, `*Digital Touch*`, or `*<app name>*` for generic apps), then the fields one per line. URLs render as Markdown autolinks `<https://…>`. Poll options render as a Markdown list with vote counts, voters nested, like TXT. Text that is already escaped or sanitized by upstream helpers is left alone; do not add a new escaping layer.
- Failure handling: if dispatch_app_balloon returns Err, fall back to exactly today's output (the message text, or `*[App message]*`). One bad balloon must never fail the export or change the function's error type for callers.
- Code location: fork-owned code only — timeline.rs, or a new fork-owned sibling file such as imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline_balloons.rs (no directory with an index/mod file). Do not edit upstream-owned files; if a trait method or helper you need is private upstream, prefer a fork-local equivalent over widening upstream visibility, and report it.
- Edited messages and stickers (named in the original bead): report what the timeline shows today for an edited message and a sticker versus what TXT shows. If the timeline drops the fact that a message was edited, append `*(edited)*` to it. Do not build full edit-history rendering.

## Out of scope
- Rendering attachments' contents, images, or HTML-style cards.
- Any change to the TXT or HTML exporters.
- A knob: Justin asked for this, and it replaces a placeholder with content (feature-knobs rule: land it on, no switch).

Unit tests in fork-owned code cover at least: URL preview (title + summary + URL), URL with no preview payload (falls back to the URL text), Apple Music, poll with votes and voters, one generic app, and the dispatch-error fallback (`*[App message]*` or the text). Build the test messages the way upstream's txt/tests/balloons.rs does (fixture plists under imessage-database/test_data/).
2. Negative control: with the App arm reverted to the old placeholder code, at least the URL, music and poll tests fail; restored, they pass.
3. Fixture smoke test: `-f timeline` on imessage-database/test_data/db/test.db exits 0; paste the lines of the output that come from app balloons (fixture data, safe to show).
4. Real-copy smoke test on the May database copy (privacy contract of imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2 applies: counts only, never message text): `-f timeline` exits 0 before and after the change, the file count is identical, and `rg -c -F '[App message]'` summed over the output drops (report before and after totals). Delete the export folders afterwards.
5. The edited-message and sticker findings are written into this bead's notes.
6. CARGO_HOME=/tmp/claude-501/cargo-home cargo build, test --workspace (0 failures), clippy --workspace --all-targets (no warnings in fork-owned files), cargo fmt --check, and `bun run signal` all pass.

title: Make the 'cannot open the Messages database' error say exactly how to fix it on macOS
description:
Make the "can't open the Messages database" error tell the user exactly what to do on macOS. Justin hit this on 2026-05-10: "I don't think the issue is full disk access -- I can access the chat.db file from the terminal." His terminal had Full Disk Access; the exporter still could not open chat.db. Upstream's message (imessage-database/src/error/table.rs, const FULL_DISK_ACCESS) only says to enable Full Disk Access for the terminal emulator, which he had already done.

## Status (2026-11-14): built and verified on worktree-upstream-5-sync in commit f2cf7624; not pushed, not merged
- New fork-owned file imessage-exporter/src/db_access_hint.rs:
  - db_access_hint(Option<PathBuf>) -> String: the pure hint builder. An empty path counts as None.
  - is_db_access_error(&RuntimeError): true only for DatabaseError(CannotConnect(Permissions(_) | Inaccessible(..))), the two variants upstream ends with its Full Disk Access line.
  - eprint_db_access_hint(&RuntimeError): holds the cfg!(target_os = "macos") gate, calls std::env::current_exe(), prints the hint to stderr.
- imessage-exporter/src/main.rs: one `mod db_access_hint;` line, and one eprint_db_access_hint(&why) call after each of the three error prints ("Invalid configuration" for Config::new, and the two "Unable to export" prints for resolve_filtered_handles and start).
- imessage-database is unchanged: git diff 47b75148 -- imessage-database is empty.

## The hint as printed (after upstream's two lines)
    If your terminal already has Full Disk Access and this still fails, add this program itself in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access:
        <absolute path from current_exe>
    Or copy the database to a folder you can read and point at the copy:
        mkdir -p /tmp/imx && cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db* /tmp/imx/
        imessage-exporter -p /tmp/imx/chat.db <your other options>
When current_exe fails or returns an empty path, the first sentence reads "... add this program itself (the imessage-exporter binary you ran) in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Full Disk Access." and no path line is printed. The hint states no cause.

## Out of scope
- Detecting Full Disk Access status programmatically (TCC queries).
- Changing upstream's message text, other error kinds, or Linux/Windows behavior.

## No knob
Message text with no sane "off" state (feature-knobs rule: no switch needed).
acceptance_criteria:
1. Unit tests for the hint builder: with Some(path) the output contains that exact path and both `-p /tmp/imx/chat.db` and the `cp ~/Library/Messages/chat.db*` line; with None it contains no empty path and names the binary in words.
2. Smoke test with the release binary on a permission-denied copy of the fixture: copy imessage-database/test_data/db/test.db to a scratch folder under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/, `chmod 000` it, run `-p <that file> -f txt -o <scratch out>`; exit code is non-zero, stderr contains upstream's original message AND the new hint with the binary's absolute path. Paste the stderr (it is fixture-derived, not personal data). Restore permissions and delete the scratch copy afterwards.
3. Negative control: with the hint call removed, the smoke test's stderr lacks the hint; restored, it has it.
4. A normal export of the fixture is unchanged (exit 0, same file count as before the change).
5. CARGO_HOME=/tmp/claude-501/cargo-home cargo build, test --workspace (0 failures), clippy --workspace --all-targets (no warnings in fork-owned files), cargo fmt --check, and `bun run signal` all pass.
6. Committed on worktree-upstream-5-sync by explicit path.
notes:
## Verification evidence (2026-11-14, commit f2cf7624)
- AC1 unit tests (db_access_hint::tests, 4 tests): with a path, the exact path is on its own line and the cp and -p /tmp/imx/chat.db lines are present; with None, the binary is named in words, no "Full Disk Access:" path intro and no blank line; an empty path gives the same text as None; the classifier is true for Inaccessible and Permissions and false for NotADatabase, QueryError and DiskError.
- AC1 negative control: breaking the path line, the empty-path filter and the Inaccessible arm failed 3 tests on exactly those assertions. Breaking the None branch failed the "names the binary in words" assertion; keeping the words but adding an empty path line failed the "hint has an empty line" assertion. Restored: 4 pass.
- AC2 smoke test: release binary, chmod 000 copy of test.db under /tmp/claude-501/imx-test/djf3/, -f txt: exit 1. stderr: upstream's "Invalid configuration: Unable to access `<copy>`: Permission denied (os error 13)" and "Ensure full disk access is enabled for your terminal emulator ..." lines, then the hint with /Users/jhaa/Dev/imessage-exporter/.claude/worktrees/upstream-5-sync/target/release/imessage-exporter. Permissions restored and the scratch folder deleted afterwards.
- AC3 negative control: with the Invalid configuration call removed, the same run exits 1 and prints only upstream's two lines (rg 'add this program itself' finds nothing). Restored: stderr byte-identical to the first run (cmp exit 0).
- AC4: a normal -f txt export of the fixture copy exits 0 with 1 file (orphaned.txt); diff -r against the pre-change baseline export is empty; no hint on stderr. A missing -p file fails earlier, in option validation, and prints no hint.
- AC5: cargo build --workspace passes; cargo test --workspace 501 + 619 + 42 passed, 0 failed (exporter was 615; +4 new); nightly-2026-08-31 clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings clean; nightly fmt --all --check clean; bun run signal passes (LINT and PRETTIER; TS not applicable); cargo build --release passes.
- AC6: committed by explicit path as f2cf7624.

## Judgment calls
- The module is at the crate root (src/db_access_hint.rs with its mod line in main.rs), not under src/app/. That keeps app/mod.rs at upstream's text: main.rs is the only upstream-owned file touched, and the fork already edits it.
- The hint call also follows the resolve_filtered_handles print (a fork-owned line). That path is not known to produce a connect error; the call is there so every RuntimeError print in main.rs behaves the same.
- The macOS gate is in eprint_db_access_hint, the helper main.rs calls, instead of being repeated at the three main.rs sites. The pure builder has no gate, so its tests run on every platform.
- Builder signature is Option<PathBuf> as scoped.
- Only the Invalid configuration branch was run end to end. The two Unable to export branches use the same helper; they are covered by construction and by the classifier test.
- The Permissions variant (SQLite open failure after the file opened) was not reproduced end to end; it is covered by the classifier test.

## Open points for the conductor
- Privacy of the copy workaround: /tmp/imx is created with the default umask (755 with umask 022), and the copied files get chat.db's mode minus the umask (not checked: ~/Library/Messages was not touched). Other local accounts may be able to read the copy. The bead fixed the two lines, so they are unchanged here. A tighter line would be `mkdir -p -m 700 /tmp/imx && ...`.
- When installed with cargo, the binary is under ~/.cargo/bin, a hidden folder; the Full Disk Access "+" file picker reaches it with Cmd+Shift+G. Not added, since it would add a fact beyond the bead.

title: Timeline export prints the chat-has-no-members warning once per message instead of once per chat
description: Found during the 5.0.1 sync smoke test (imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2). On the May real-database copy, -f timeline wrote the upstream warning 'Found error: message chat ID N has no members!' 991 times to stderr; -f txt and -f html wrote it once. Cause: chat_display_label in imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs calls Config::filename for every collected message, and Config::filename prints that warning each time it runs for a chat with no participants. The txt/html driver memoizes the filename per chat (ExportState.route), so it prints once. Fix shape: cache the thread label per chat rowid inside Timeline (a HashMap<i32, String>), so Config::filename runs once per chat. Fork-owned code only; do not change Config::filename (upstream-owned).
acceptance_criteria: 1. A unit test in timeline.rs shows chat_display_label/Config::filename runs once per chat across many messages of that chat (e.g. a counter or a cached-label assertion). 2. On the May real-db copy (privacy contract of imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2: counts only), rg -c of 'has no members' in the -f timeline stderr equals the -f txt count (1 on 2026-11-14). 3. The timeline file's day/thread/message header counts are unchanged versus before the fix. 4. cargo build, test --workspace, clippy, fmt check and bun run signal pass.

Keep the edit small and in one place so future upstream syncs conflict as little as possible. The sync bead lists the timeline / -w documentation in imessage-exporter/README.md as an allowed fork-owned difference.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The -f line and the -w block in the README's help listing match target/release/imessage-exporter --help output exactly. 2. One example each for -f timeline and -w. 3. git diff --stat 47b75148 HEAD -- imessage-exporter/README.md shows only these additions. 4. bun run signal passes (the README stays in .prettierignore). 5. Committed by explicit path.

title: Keep the timeline export going when one message cannot be read, the way the txt and html exports do
description: In imessage-exporter/src/exporters/timeline.rs, format_timeline_message uses ? on Attachment::from_message and msg.get_replies, so one unreadable message aborts the whole timeline export. Upstream's shared driver (exporters/shared/driver.rs) used by txt and html logs such a message and continues. Found by the 2026-11-14 upstream-sync review; the May database copy hit no such error, so this is a robustness fix, not an observed failure.
acceptance_criteria: A per-message error in the timeline exporter is reported on stderr with the message id and the export continues; a unit or fixture test forces the error and proves the export still finishes; negative control shown.

title: bun run signal fails after cargo doc because eslint lints the generated target/doc JavaScript
description: Found 2026-11-14 during imessage-exporter-3p0.1.2. Running upstream's CI check 'RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps --workspace' writes rustdoc JavaScript into target/doc. eslint.config.cjs ignores only tmp/, dist/ and .claude/worktrees/, so the next 'bun run signal' fails LINT with about 1,670 problems, all under target/doc. target/ is Cargo's build directory (git-ignored) and holds no source to lint. Fix shape: add 'target/' to the ignores array in eslint.config.cjs (fork-owned tooling). If justin-sdk generates this config for Rust repos, the better home is the justin-sdk template, so other Rust repos get it too.
acceptance_criteria: 1. After 'cargo doc --no-deps --workspace' leaves target/doc in place, 'bun run signal' passes. 2. Negative control: without the ignore entry, the same sequence fails LINT. 3. Committed by explicit path.
